features.title: Source text and lexical forms
pending: Invalid UTF-8 source and diagnostic positions; CRLF and source normalization
Remaining reserved contexts and malformed literal contracts
features.note: ASCII callable suffixes, reserved declarations/parameters/members/argument labels and maximal operator tokens are covered across ordinary execution and retained REPL state. Type parsing preserves nested generic angles and later origins. Symbols and Hash labels retain literal names; reserved value names cannot resolve. The pinned reference also rejects an adjacent bang/equality spelling. Unicode identifiers and remaining lexical boundaries stay open.

features.title: Strings and UTF-8
pending: Reference output-mode Unicode case differences (TypeRB #791)
Embedded-expression boundaries beyond the reviewed interpolation probes
features.note: Ordinary UTF-8 literals, code-point size/index, collections and NUL/long data are covered. Additional CLI tests cover argv, invalid source, forced GC and terminal editing. String empty/include/start/end queries and nullable first/last search now share code-point offsets, argument ordering, optional receivers and managed lifetime checks. Split, literal replace_all and Unicode simple upcase/downcase now have checked MIR, byte-level, lifetime and retained-session coverage. Reference output-mode case differences remain explicit. Chars, codepoints and reverse preserve code-point units, independent result storage, NUL, optional receivers and managed lifetimes. String slice now accepts checked code-point ranges, retaining receiver identity and optional short circuit; negative, reversed and out-of-bounds ranges fail explicitly. Control, octal, hex and scalar Unicode escapes preserve exact bytes, reject invalid scalar/digit forms and do not recursively start interpolation. Strip, lstrip and rstrip use the reference Unicode White_Space set, preserve retained bytes and manage optional, generic, captured and stored values.

features.title: Immutable Bytes
pending: Bytes values across remaining nominal wrappers and imported declarations
features.note: String#to_bytes and Bytes size, strict unsigned at, immutable concat, valid_utf8? and maximal-subpart replacement to_s use distinct typed MIR. Shared ordinary and retained REPL probes cover empty/NUL/multibyte input, all 256 byte values, malformed prefixes, scalar boundaries, split-sequence concatenation, class/record fields, generic calls, Array/Hash, nullable values, closures, Any output and argument order. Construction, mutation, equality and invalid method arguments remain rejected as in the pinned reference. Binary encoding and service adapters are separate package work.

features.title: Numeric and Boolean operations
pending: Remaining operators and assignment forms; mixed widening and portable failure boundaries
Lazy evaluation with remaining transfer, nullable invalidation and projection combinations
features.note: Integer and Float receiver operations, scalar String conversion, Float output and Integer/Float power use typed MIR. Power is right-associative with unary precedence below it; checked Integer multiplication preserves the portable range. Shared probes cover numeric limits, subnormals, signed zero, NaN, infinities, optional calls, constants and managed captures. Broader numeric APIs and exact shortest-decimal REPL inspection at rare rounding boundaries remain open. Lazy Boolean and compound-assignment cases cover effect order through locals, globals, captures, class fields and Array elements, nested controls and RHS return, managed String updates, saved Array values/positions and rejected operands or targets. Readonly record fields remain rejected.

features.title: Bindings, constants and mutation
pending: Remaining collection-inference combinations; qualified namespace binding members (TypeRB #787)
features.note: File/project and interactive lowercase variables preserve source identity, shared mutable storage, lexical shadowing, nullable proof invalidation and managed roots. Block declarations may shadow enclosing locals in conditional and collection bodies while duplicate declarations, parameter redeclarations and while-body shadowing are rejected. Retained named functions and anonymous captures share cells; typed witnesses never rerun initializers. Authored order survives load/replay. Unit-local import cycles use a verified value dependency order, with source diagnostics for initialization cycles and opaque calls; acyclic order is preserved. Mutable record projections accept indexed Array writes and growth; immutable projections reject writes. Empty Array and Hash constants have reference-matching untyped boundaries; fresh mutable bindings use exact contexts and first-statement write constraints, including literal fn bodies. Nested and sibling closures retain lexical ownership, later writes cannot widen the type, and unresolved aliases/escapes require annotations. Qualified lowercase namespace-member access remains pending.

features.title: Function declarations and calls
features.note: Explicit return paths cover guards, nested branches, cases, loops, nonlocal iteration transfers and rejected completing paths. Nested calls preserve left-to-right, exactly-once evaluation, short-circuit transfers and managed argument lifetimes. Parameter mutability is local to the implementation binding: rebinding does not replace the caller binding, while shared Array identity survives calls and projections. Retained REPL submissions and immutable-parameter diagnostics are reviewed separately.

features.title: Defaults and named arguments
pending: Imported method-default shadowing across execution modes (reference issue #1134)
features.note: Positional and named-only defaults have declaration-scoped, typed MIR initializer bodies. Explicit expressions precede omitted defaults; checking and the REPL share binding identities. Instance, class and concrete generic methods preserve receiver-before-argument evaluation, written explicit-argument order, fresh mutable defaults and earlier-parameter dependencies. Required callable parameters, explicit fn adapters and positional-only invocation are checked separately from named declarations; mutable scalar parameter rebinding stays local. Payload-enum constructors admit required positional and named-only fields, preserving written evaluation order across concrete generics, nullable payloads and imported aliases. Missing, extra, duplicate, unknown, misplaced and mistyped arguments are rejected; payload defaults remain rejected as specified.

features.title: Conditions and value-producing branches
pending: Nullable/union common result types and broader expression nesting boundaries
features.note: Value branches have typed MIR joins, numeric widening and lexical transfer propagation; shared probes cover effects, scope and managed aliases.

features.title: Loop control and transfers
pending: Additional nested transfer and diagnostic-origin differential probes
features.note: Conditional return, break and next evaluate the guard first and share lexical targets with MIR and the REPL.

features.title: Case statements and expressions
features.note: Integer and String literal alternatives and exhaustive enum cases are supported; non-exhaustive value-producing cases require else. The pinned reference includes the open scalar case fix from type-rb/type-rb#826, so its unmatched scalar cases continue like Native's.

features.title: Records and field bindings
pending: Nominal cycles and defaults involving remaining unsupported value types
features.note: Generic and ordinary defaults share declaration-scoped initializers; explicit fields run before omitted defaults, with fresh managed values and independent concrete type instances. Same-named records in separate namespaces retain nominal identities, generic fields, defaults and import aliases; matching shapes and unrelated class members do not confer compatibility.

features.title: Member access and projections
pending: Safe member access, chained field narrowing and receiver replacement
features.note: Object-field comparisons retain ordinary operator parsing and checked projection in compiled execution and retained REPL values.

features.title: Nullable values and narrowing
pending: Class/callback and general pattern narrowing; remaining collection/union optional conversions; unguarded nullable indexing (issue #1120)
Nullable standard-library methods beyond the currently implemented Native APIs
features.note: Native uses explicit typed none/present/test/extraction MIR with traced payload storage and checked extraction. Direct lexical/stable record-field guards, returning guards, short-circuit RHS and safe navigation are covered; chained predicates do not export extra narrowing facts. Retained REPL assignments use checked exit facts; partial failure and interruption clear earlier narrowing. Conditional/failure probes expose known bugs in the fixed reference revision, and statement-control result display remains different. Optional scalar output uses verified branches and payload extraction and matches current reference output separately for ordinary execution and the REPL. Fresh mutable empty collections infer nullable declarations from exact typed contexts before ordinary checking. Call/return/alias/assignment/nested/generic/closure cases cover guards, lexical inference regions, blocked escapes, managed aliases and retained REPL types. Nullable Hash Go-lowering failures in the pinned reference and the separate unguarded-index boundary remain explicit (type-rb-native#1120).

features.title: Enums and tagged values
pending: Method-specific type parameters, attribute output-mode effects and remaining pattern/control combinations
Reference REPL initializer replay (TypeRB #768) and shadowed standard error identity (#769); imported/nested REPL presentation parity
features.note: Ordinary/raw/payload enums, explicit String/Integer representations, checked Result conversions and instance methods use verified MIR. Generic enum receiver arguments specialize defaults, recursive/private calls and closures before MIR catalogs freeze. Declaration attributes retain checked metadata without executing their arguments. Shared and retained-session cases cover aliases, imports, nullable calls and rejected templates. Method-specific parameters, output-mode attribute effects, reference defects and display gaps remain explicit. Explicit generic pattern owners consume canonical checked types, including nested/function type arguments, generic bodies, aliases and imports, while preserving payload labels, branch scope and exhaustiveness. Plain payloadless enum output uses declaration ordinals in compiled execution and retains symbolic REPL presentation, including imported and generic calls.

features.title: Transparent aliases
pending: Authored alias spelling in diagnostics, nominal import display and nullable union alternative ordering (#455)
Transparent alias compatibility at conditional branch joins (proposal #1128)
features.note: Transparent and generic aliases resolve to canonical checked types before MIR. Literal union targets retain constraints through alias chains, generic applications, nullable and collection contexts, defaults, qualified names and renamed imports. Generic record and readonly class union targets preserve discriminant narrowing and reject invalid literals, wide values, mismatched payloads, unguarded fields and incomplete cases. Enum alias names survive checked REPL inference, copies, containers, constants and matching control branches; explicit contexts and projections retain canonical semantics. Existing probes also cover recursive targets, declaration scope, Result, patterns, function signatures, imported interface conformance, newtype wrapping and canonical class identity. Diagnostic and REPL presentation differences and pinned reference branch-join defects (#1128) remain explicit.

features.title: Nominal newtypes
pending: Class/interface representation dependencies
Method references and wider callable/generic combinations
features.note: Explicit nominal construction/projection and open or closed methods preserve identity through aliases, imports, managed values, nullable calls, captures and MIR storage erasure. Independent verification and ordinary/retained-session cases cover representation, lifetime and rejection boundaries. Printable scalar union output is supported; Hash presentation differences remain explicit. Method-specific generic parameters use explicit receivers and concrete checked specializations across ordinary execution and REPL; cases cover recursion, forwarding, defaults, callbacks, captures, nullable results, imports and nominal/privacy/arity rejection boundaries.

features.title: Generic declarations and applications
pending: Remaining method-specific generic combinations and deferred generic class methods; enum ordinary/REPL contract decision (#1160)
Wider constraints and type applications
Generic output of concrete aggregate values
Nullable type-argument output differs from the reference Go representation (#691)
features.note: Explicit record/enum and top-level function applications use concrete checked MIR. Function templates and record/parameter defaults are checked even when unused. Imported generic enum identity, local shadowing and full control defaults agree with the updated reference; remaining Hash REPL display differences stay explicit. Concrete class and interface applications, generic fields and explicit instance-method parameters also use checked MIR. Output in checked function templates is accepted before concrete scalar, nullable, union, Bytes and Any instantiations are lowered to verified MIR. Present nullable type arguments expose a reference Go output discrepancy (#691); the finite Bytes difference is registered, while unstable address output is retained in the proposal reproduction.

features.title: Union values, literal types and discriminated unions
pending: Reference grouped annotation and nullable-alternative boundaries (TypeRB #764 and #765); composite type patterns remain staged in the reference
features.note: General and literal unions compose with collections, optional values, generics, aliases, nominal payloads, Results and closures through verified MIR. Singleton constraints widen explicitly; literal cases, common record/class data members and callable fields and overlapping discriminants preserve exhaustive checking and mutation invalidation. Homogeneous literal-union Hash keys retain typed identity through value-based lookup, copies and snapshots. Readonly class discriminants preserve overlapping alternatives, generic/imported identities and existing shallow field capabilities. The pinned reference and Native reject private union fields and execute common class-union field writes through variant-specific verified MIR. REPL presentation differences remain.

features.title: Function values and lexical capture
pending: Method references and remaining parameter-capability/narrowing combinations
features.note: Ordinary files and retained REPL submissions construct anonymous and named function values using concrete checked bodies and their originating code/type catalogs. Required positional named declarations preserve import identity, lexical shadowing, managed storage, nullable narrowing, Result obligations and generic type applications. Defaults, named-only and generic declarations require explicit fn adapters. CLI controls additionally cover cross-submission calls, failures, collection and replay. Other boundaries and diagnostic differences remain explicit. Literal fn bodies constrain captured fresh mutable Arrays and Hashes before ordinary capture checking, including deferred and returned closures, concrete generics, numeric common types and union values. Retained REPL cells preserve shared payload identity. Dedicated controls reject function equality and ordering, preserve nullable absence tests and distinguish immutable capture proofs from mutable captures requiring an inner guard. Array arguments, readonly parameter rejection, function-type aliases and higher-order calls retain the pinned parameter behavior.

features.title: Arrays and checked indexes
pending: Remaining receiver and inference combinations; unguarded nullable indexing (issue #1120)
Wider invalid element/mutation combinations
features.note: Array edges/copies/slicing, mutable insertion/removal, scalar/payloadless equality queries, uniqueness, shallow concatenation and String joining share typed MIR and REPL behavior. Cases cover retained receivers, argument effects, nullable calls, managed aliases, Unicode/NUL, NaN and signed zero. Remaining methods and diagnostic differences stay explicit. Stable non-destructive sort/sort_descending support non-nullable Integer/Float/String elements, with NaNs last in both directions, signed-zero stability and byte-preserving Unicode order. Rare Float shortest-decimal ties, nominal literal-type labels and inline callable-array reading remain explicit REPL differences. sort_by/sort_by_descending retain visited values and evaluate one portable Integer/Float/String key per element. Safe block navigation remains an explicit reference defect (type-rb/type-rb#774). Fresh mutable empty Arrays accept concrete and nullable call, return, assignment, alias and nested literal contexts. Nullable constraints govern the original declaration and survive generic/closure checking and retained REPL submissions; untyped escapes and conflicting later writes remain invalid. Literal closures contribute push/unshift writes and exact contexts in the binding's first constraining statement, including nested and sibling closures. Empty replacement literals leave pending REPL bindings unresolved until a later constraint.

features.title: Hash values and operations
pending: Wider key/value representations, dynamic Any operations, remaining inference combinations and managed lifetimes; nullable Hash reference Go lowering and unguarded indexing (issue #1120)
features.note: Colon keys support quoted and computed String keys, Integer keys and parenthesized identifier labels, retaining authored key/value evaluation order. Boolean and nil keys remain rejected. Homogeneous Integer/String literal-union keys use payload equality while snapshots preserve the exact key type. Growth, deletion, copies, nullable refinement and managed lifetimes are covered; mixed and nullable keys remain rejected. Fresh mutable empty Hashes accept concrete and nullable call, return, assignment and nested literal contexts, preserving key types and managed value aliases. The pinned reference accepts nullable Hash contexts in checking/REPL but fails Go builds; those path-specific failures and the unguarded-index boundary remain recorded (type-rb-native#1120). Literal closure index writes and update calls infer homogeneous keys and common/union value types in the first owning statement. Shared captures, later-write rejection and pending empty replacements are exercised across ordinary execution and retained REPL submissions.

features.title: Structured and value-producing iteration
pending: Remaining receiver APIs that shorten or reorder an Array during traversal
features.note: Array and Range each/map/select/reduce use shared checked statement bodies and ordinary MIR loops. Transforms retain one receiver, observe live Array growth/replacement, preserve visited selection values and evaluate reduce initializers before traversal. Indexed map/select and managed captures are covered. Short-circuit any?/all?/none? retain the same live source, require Boolean results and lower early exits to ordinary MIR edges. find/find_index retain visited values and produce checked nullable results with short-circuit exits. Hash each snapshots keys and values before its body; insertion, deletion, rebinding, managed aliases and loop transfers are covered without promising enumeration order. Array sort_by/sort_by_descending collect retained values and keys once through the same live iteration, then stably sort paired private buffers through ordinary MIR control flow.

features.title: Range values and boundaries
features.note: Materialization shares each endpoint rules, creates a fresh Array and exits before incrementing an inclusive portable maximum.

features.title: Result and typed propagation
pending: General union errors and compiler-declared structured package boundaries
features.note: Compiler-owned Result/Unit, ordinary case/try/catch, required-use and managed payloads use existing verified enum/control MIR. REPL controls cover automatic roots, aliases, retained values and reload. Optional error widening exposes a fixed-reference build/REPL defect; current reference main handles it correctly.

features.title: Classes, fields and methods
pending: Initialized superclass storage and constructor chaining; inherited overrides (TypeRB #797)
features.note: Ordinary constructors, field defaults, scalar/managed/generic fields, instance/class/private methods, readonly initialization and field-free inheritance use verified MIR. Qualified classes, imported parents and inherited constants preserve lexical owners. The retained REPL preserves aliases, captures and replay. Shared negative observations retain diagnostic differences. Class aliases construct their canonical targets through the same checked allocation and constructor path. Lexical class self dispatches static methods and constructors in ordinary execution and the retained REPL. Common class-union field stores select the receiver before the RHS and write through verified alternative-specific MIR. Object-field comparisons retain ordinary operator parsing and checked projection in compiled execution and retained REPL values.

features.title: Explicit interface conformance
pending: Variance and method-specific generic contracts with the reference object specification
Initialized-superclass and override dependencies
features.note: Explicit and inherited nominal conformance, generic interface applications, heterogeneous interface Arrays and dynamic calls use independently verified method witnesses and managed boxes. Namespace/import aliases preserve contract identity and callable results. Missing methods, wrong signatures, implicit conformance and interface construction reject.

features.title: Modules and constant lookup
pending: Remaining module method and qualified mutable namespace-member boundaries
features.note: Nested/reopened namespaces, lexical privacy, ordered runtime constants, imported inferred types and qualified generic aliases are implemented. Cyclic source modules use the checked initialization plan while same-file value order remains enforced. Reference issues #755 and #756 remain explicit boundaries; classes belong to the object-declaration family.

features.title: Symbol values
pending: Remaining reference operator/control framing and multiline interpolation boundaries
features.note: Portable identifier and quoted Symbol spellings are String values. Shared cases cover equality, methods, defaults, generic/optional values, captures and storage. Both quote styles retain interpolation-looking contents literally; parser-selected normalization preserves Hash/named-argument context. Keyword Symbols also frame correctly in the REPL. Remaining operator/control framing and multiline interpolation gaps stay explicit. Maximal operator spelling, callable-suffix names and reserved Hash/Symbol labels are covered; Hash REPL ordering/format differences remain visible.

features.title: Project imports and declaration identity
pending: Bare/named aliases, graph conflicts, missing/unused imports and file/project/REPL identity
features.note: Named aliases, automatic project imports, record binding identity and standard-package aliases have ordinary probes; broader import and diagnostic contracts remain. Retained nominal values preserve declaration ownership and concrete generic arguments even without a visible type import or when another module declares the same name. Ambiguous bare class/interface roots are rejected; project-startup versus interactive-submission exit status remains a REPL parity gap.

features.title: Target source interop
pending: Go/Ruby/TypeScript source emission and platform interop
features.note: A later toolchain contract is required; these remain project goals, not basic Native support claims.

features.title: Portable HTTP values
pending: Networking, streaming, transport adapters and Web semantic/type providers
features.note: Pinned Body, Header, Headers, HeaderValueError and HttpMethod values cover raw bytes, ordered case-insensitive headers, typed lookup failures, immutable snapshots, imports and retained REPL ownership. These value contracts do not establish an HTTP client or server.

features.title: Web values and middleware
pending: HTTP serving and whole-buffer gzip have dedicated runtime acceptance; logger, timeout and authentication providers remain incomplete
features.note: Pinned Request, Response, cookies and ContextKey values support ordinary imports and retained REPL ownership. Portable middleware composes ordered handlers with once-only Next calls. Browser middleware covers actual/preflight CORS negotiation, origin and credential rules, header reflection and retention, security-header configuration, and composition short circuits. A file-route integration combines RequestID, security headers and CORS across GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, missing and malformed paths under forced collection. These checks do not establish networking or the remaining host-backed providers.

features.title: JSX and web bindings
pending: Typed JSX and official web-package boundaries
features.note: Requires the source backend and web package contracts; remains in the complete toolchain goal.

features.title: Package capability activation
pending: Package-owned activation and resolution
features.note: Requires package resolution and its capability contract; remains in the complete toolchain goal.

features.title: Retired authored attempt syntax
features.note: The reference AST retains this node for pre-0.3 recovery; authored attempt syntax is rejected, not a language capability to implement.

features.title: JSON values and comments
pending: Generic record schemas remain incomplete
Deterministic precedence for multiple invalid object members requires the decision in #1138
features.note: Pinned JSON/JSONC declarations expose recursive values, strict and comment-aware parsing, deterministic serialization, typed accessors and field lookup through owned TypeRB adapters. Ordinary file/project and retained REPL paths preserve source ownership, nominal identities and managed values. Error precedence for multiple invalid object members differs in the pinned reference; #1138 records that ambiguity.

features.title: Typed Web path and query records
pending: Integer-backed raw enums and multiple non-nullable Array fields await a cross-mode reference decision (#1175)
Time range, parsing and codec-import restrictions remain tracked in the time-services family
features.note: Loader-owned providers specialize Context#params<T> and Request#query<T> for canonical record fields through ordinary checked TypeRB bodies and verified MIR. Scalars, string-backed enums, portable time types, nullable fields and query Arrays preserve field order, repeated values and typed missing/duplicate/invalid errors; multiple arrays are admitted when at most one is non-nullable. Cross-module aliases, retained REPL records and managed lifetimes remain on the ordinary path. Reference inconsistencies stay visible instead of defining a Native-only contract.

features.title: Typed JSON codecs and Web JSON
pending: Generic record schemas remain incomplete; recursive schemas and closed inbound newtypes retain the reference rejection
Response.json REPL invocation awaits the adapter decision in #1178
Non-finite JSON error message differs between compiled and REPL reference paths; #1179 owns the unresolved parity gap
features.note: Canonical loader-owned JSON.decode<T>, JSON.encode, Request#json<T> and Response.json generate ordinary checked TypeRB bodies and verified MIR. Finite record schemas compose nullable fields, arrays, string-keyed hashes, raw enums, the six portable time types, open newtype decoding, newtype encoding and JSON wire names. Structured field errors, content-type/UTF-8 request checks, response status/fallback, once-only evaluation, cross-module aliases, retained REPL values and managed lifetimes have bounded probes. Typed providers produce ordinary TypeRB bodies; time host dependencies and remaining time parity gaps are tracked by the time-services family.

features.title: Combined Web endpoint inputs
pending: Renamed imported envelope records remain rejected pending canonical-identity decision #1183
Calling bind without a type argument is rejected; reference check-only acceptance differs and awaits #1184
HTTP server lifecycle remains incomplete; typed Context storage is tracked by the web-context family
features.note: Canonical Context#bind<T> composes checked path, query and JSON providers for nonempty records containing params, query and body sections. Evaluation follows that fixed order and preserves the first original typed error. Bounded probes cover omitted sections, nested values, local aliases and canonical imports, once-only receiver evaluation, catch/try composition, retained REPL records and forced-GC lifetimes. Source-erased MIR, signature tampering, provider ownership and speculative-fork immutability are checked independently. No backend adapter, public syntax or reference pin is changed.

features.title: Portable time values and Web time codecs
pending: Portable constructor/parser bounds and Duration integer limits await consistent reference semantics (#1187)
TimeOfDay/DateTime error prefixes and Duration leading-plus parsing differ between reference execution modes (#1188)

Renamed time codec imports retain the reference restriction pending #1189; implicitly required but otherwise unused imports also intersect #1180. Project-startup versus interactive-submission rejection remains an imports-family REPL gap
System zone data is required; TZ/ZONEINFO overrides, zip or embedded databases, TZif v4 and broader environment parity remain unqualified
Monotonic clocks and scheduling remain incomplete
features.note: The unchanged pinned Date, TimeOfDay, DateTime, Instant, Duration and TimeZone wrappers use ordinary TypeRB calendar, parser, formatting, TZif and POSIX-footer implementations. Bounded probes cover negative epochs, leap boundaries, nanoseconds, negative durations, named zones, historical/future offsets, ambiguous and nonexistent local times, JSON and Web inputs, canonical aliases, retained REPL identities and forced-GC lifetimes. Two verified host adapters transfer wall-clock integers and bounded zone-file bytes; independent MIR checks reject ownership, signature and effect tampering. Full time-service parity remains incomplete.

features.title: Typed Web context values
pending: REPL binding display of opaque Context storage awaits the portable inspection decision in #1192; deterministic value-operation probes do not establish display parity
features.note: Canonical ContextKey<T> instances identify typed entries. Checked Context.with/fetch preserve value types, immutable branches, evaluation order and ordinary aliasing; with_request carries state and path parameters into the replacement request. Public scalar, aggregate, nominal, generic and nullable fixtures exercise compiled and retained REPL values with independent source-erased MIR, provider ownership and forced-GC checks. Callable-body observations avoid nondeterministic host address dumps; the separate binding-display difference remains explicit.

features.title: Hex, Base64 and secure random bytes
pending: Host-failure diagnostic equivalence across implementations remains unqualified
features.note: Pinned Hex/Base64 wrappers retain canonical error types and strict validation order through private TypeRB implementations. Shared cases cover binary round trips, Unicode error positions, canonical padding bits, aliases, secure-random bounds and RequestID middleware propagation. The owned entropy bridge uses OS bytes without a weak fallback; deterministic OS-shim checks qualify Native chunk bounds and failure behavior separately. Other cryptographic packages and Web routing remain separate work.

features.title: File routes and in-process Web dispatch
pending: Network serving, streaming, cancellation and shutdown remain incomplete
Wider generic and helper schema combinations remain unqualified
features.note: Configured application routes cover static precedence, dynamic and catch-all paths, canonical handler signatures, path-name/schema validation, root/nested middleware, request normalization, HEAD/OPTIONS, 404/405/413 and invalid responses. Project startup validates routes for the REPL without requiring main; dispatch execution itself preserves the pinned reference REPL restriction. Ordinary generated TypeRB composes handlers above MIR; a cross-module RequestID/typed-Context/JSON integration checks managed lifetimes. Owned recovery covers handler, nested/root middleware and double-Next failures, preserves preceding effects and root continuation, suppresses HEAD bodies and permits later healthy requests. Forced collection checks repeated recovery and captured managed values. These probes do not establish network cancellation, complete Web or release parity.

features.title: Checked endpoint declarations and Web generators
pending: Ordinary unowned class-body calls remain incomplete pending #1208; local namesakes, indirect descendants and namespaced contracts are explicit gaps
Entry-free configured project checking remains incomplete; the pinned OpenAPI command itself requires a main entry
Native source-backend execution and server lifecycle remain incomplete
Pinned browser-client consumer type identity failures remain explicit under #1183 and #1212; generator ownership review is #1211
features.note: Top-level direct loader-owned Endpoint declarations resolve local handlers, marker signatures, canonical input/response types, declaration counts and literal status codes without adding executable calls. Ordinary checking, builds, execution and retained REPL loading share the checked catalog. OpenAPI generation separately qualifies deterministic paths, parameters, JSON bodies, named components, wire names, nullable/collection/nominal/time shapes and generation-only errors. Browser-client generation preserves shared imports, typed status results, path/query/body encoding and explicit request failures. CLI integration covers deterministic reference source output, all modes, output replacement, toolchain independence and error preservation; separate reference browser projections and synthetic Fetch transport tests qualify generated consumers. Pinned spelling-sensitive scalar behavior remains unchanged pending #1207. This family does not establish complete Web or release parity.

features.title: Path and validated relative path values
features.note: The pinned portable Path, RelativePath and RelativePathError value API is available through ordinary checking, builds, execution and retained REPL loading. POSIX Path#join preserves parent bytes; validated relative composition, error precedence, Unicode, aliases, generics, imported functions, collections and nominal/private-constructor rejection match the reference. Forced collection separately checks retained managed values. Filesystem I/O, additional target platforms and source-backend execution remain separate coverage work.

features.title: Scoped File and ambient directory operations
pending: Opened directory capabilities and cooperative lock scopes remain separate coverage work
Concurrent-map resource effects remain unqualified because Native rejects the concurrent_map syntax before effect checking
Pinned reference REPL implicit-import replay remains visible in the directory case under #1127; directory multi-error ordering review is #1287
Complete four-host release qualification and source-backend execution remain outstanding
features.note: Loader-owned File.open checks immutable synchronous borrows and a structured Result boundary; bounded byte/text reads and writes, UTF-8/BOM handling, ambient directory enumeration/creation and retained REPL values share canonical path/error identities. The focused filesystem acceptance separately covers exclusive creation, symlinks/nonregular handles, limits, nested scopes, resource escape, forced collection and injected cleanup failures. Header ABI qualification is separate from ordinary target execution. These probes do not establish anchored containment, locks or full release parity.

features.title: Buffered string construction
pending: Aliased new factory code generation in the pinned reference.
Generic collection display containing builders.
Explicit puts across compiled execution and REPL: specification proposal #1249; current mode-specific reference behavior is preserved.
features.note: Canonical factories and primitive methods preserve shared mutation, immutable snapshots, split UTF-8 fragments, Unicode counts and clear/reuse. Ordinary paths have separate expectations; dedicated runtime tests cover growth, forced GC, invalid code points, private span bounds and retained REPL values. The pinned REPL prints the inspected builder form, while compiled puts prints its text; both mode-specific behaviors are preserved.

features.title: OIDC Bearer authentication
pending: Complete transport edge compatibility and release artifact qualification.
features.note: Shared ordinary cases record pre-network configuration and missing-credential behavior. HTTPS discovery/JWKS, RS256, claims, proxy/trust/redirect policy, middleware context and cache/GC/failure behavior use the dedicated synthetic provider corpus in tools/native-oidc-test.py. The retained REPL follows the reference unavailable-adapter diagnostic; these examples do not establish complete package or release parity.

	return values.size().to_s() + ":" + values[0]
end

def select(first: Integer, second: Integer = first + 1, *, third: Integer = second + 1): Integer
	return first * 100 + second * 10 + third
end

def fresh_hash(mut values: Hash<String, Array<String>> = { "key" =>["kept"] }): Integer
	mut items := values["key"]
	items.push("grown")
	return items.size()
end

record Entry
	first: String
	second: String = trace("default-second", first)
	items: Array<String> = [second]
	count: Float = items.size()
end

def identity(*, entry: Entry = Entry.new(first: trace("default-first", "record"))): Entry
	return entry
end

def lazy(value: Boolean = false && (1 / 0 == 0)): Boolean
	return value
end

def probe()
	puts(collect())
	puts(collect())
	mut values := ["explicit"]
	puts(collect(values, label: trace("explicit-label", "later")))
	puts(values.size())
	puts(select(1))

	puts(select(1, 4))

	puts(first.count.to_i())

	puts(items.size())
	puts(third.items.size())
	puts(third.items[0])
	puts(lazy())

cases.title: Brace iteration with nested controls and lexical transfers
cases.declarations:
def probe(): Integer
	mut values := ["a", "b" + "b"]
	mut total := 0
	values.each.with_index { |value, index|
		if index == 0
			values.push("c" + "cc")
			next
		end
		(1..3).each { |step|
			if step == 2
				next
			end
			mut turn := 0
			while turn < 3
				turn += 1
				break if turn == 2
				total += value.size() + index + step
			end
			break if step == 3
		}
		if index == 2
			return total
		end
	}
	return - 1
end

def brace_controls()
	puts(probe())
	[1, 2].each { |value| if value == 1; puts("first"); else; puts("second"); end }

cases.title: Short-circuit Array and Range predicates and boundary values
cases.declarations:
def probe()
	empty: Array<Integer> := []
	missing := empty.any? { |item| item > 0 }
	complete := empty.all? { |item| item > 0 }
	absent := empty.none? { |item| item > 0 }
	puts(missing)
	puts(complete)
	puts(absent)
	mut visits := 0
	found := [1, 2, 3].any? do |item|
		visits += 1
		item == 2
	end
	puts(found)
	puts(visits)
	visits = 0
	every := [1, 2, 3].all?() do |item|
		visits += 1
		item < 2
	end
	puts(every)
	puts(visits)
	visits = 0
	no_match := [1, 2, 3].none? do |item|
		visits += 1
		item == 2
	end
	puts(no_match)
	puts(visits)
	all_small := [1, 2].all? { |item| item < 3 }
	none_small := [1, 2].none? { |item| item > 3 }
	any_large := [1, 2].any? { |item| item > 3 }
	puts(all_small)
	puts(none_small)
	puts(any_large)
	maximum := (9007199254740991..9007199254740991).all? { |item| item > 0 }
	excluded := (9007199254740991...9007199254740991).any? { |item| item > 0 }
	reversed := (3..1).none? { |item| item > 0 }
	puts(maximum)
	puts(excluded)
	puts(reversed)
	# Stop after the second element.
	finite := (1..3).any? { |item| item == 2 }
	puts(finite)
	mut outer := 0
	nested := [1, 2].all? do |item|
		outer += 1
		answer := (1..3).any? { |other| item == other }
		answer
	end
	puts(nested)
	puts(outer)
	# Lazy evaluation must skip the zero divisor after the first match.
	lazy := [1, 0].any? { |item| 10 / item > 0 }
	puts(lazy)
end

def matches<T>(values: Array<T>, predicate: (T) -> Boolean): Boolean
	return values.any? { |item| predicate(item) }
end

def source(mut events: Array<Integer>, values: Array<Integer>): Array<Integer>
	events.push(1)
	return values
end

def probe()
	mut values := [1, 2]
	mut retained := values
	readonly := retained
	mut events: Array<Integer> := []
	found := source(events, readonly).any? do |item|
		events.push(item)
		if item == 1
			retained.push(3)
			retained[1] = 20
			values = [99]
		end
		item == 3
	end
	puts(found)
	puts(events.size())
	puts(events[2])
	puts(events[3])
	puts(values[0])
	mut captured: Array<() -> String> := []
	labels := ["first" + 1.to_s(), "target" + 2.to_s(), "unvisited"]
	selected := labels.any? do |label|
		callback := fn(): String
			return label
		end
		captured.push(callback)
		label = label + "!"
		label == "target2!"
	end
	puts(selected)
	puts(captured.size())
	puts(captured[0]())
	puts(captured[1]())
	predicate := fn(value: String): Boolean
		return value == "target2"
	end
	puts(matches<String>(labels, predicate))
	checker := fn(values: Array<Integer>): Boolean
		return values.none? { |item| item == 0 }
	end
	puts(checker([1, 2]))
end

record Entry
	name: String
end

def first<T>(values: Array<T>, predicate: (T) -> Boolean): T?
	return values.find { |item| predicate(item) }

def probe()
	mut source := [Entry.new(name: "original" + 1.to_s())]
	selected := source.find do |item|
		source[0] = Entry.new(name: "replacement")
		item = Entry.new(name: "parameter")
		item.name == "parameter"
	end
	if selected != nil
		puts(selected.name)
	end
	mut values := [1, 2]
	mut retained := values
	mut calls := 0
	index := values.find_index do |item|
		calls += 1
		if item == 1
			retained[1] = 20
			retained.push(3)
			values = [99]
		end
		item == 3
	end
	if index != nil
		puts(index)
	end
	puts(calls)
	puts(values[0])
	mut callbacks: Array<() -> String> := []
	text := ["first" + 1.to_s(), "second" + 2.to_s()].find do |item|
		callback := fn(): String
			return item
		end
		callbacks.push(callback)
		item = item + "!"
		item == "second2!"
	end
	if text != nil
		puts(text)
	end
	puts(callbacks[1]())
	predicate := fn(value: String): Boolean
		return value == "generic"
	end
	result := first<String>(["generic"], predicate)
	if result != nil
		puts(result)
	end
end

def optional_absolute(value: Integer?): Integer?
	return value&.abs()
end

def record_value(mut events: Array<Integer>, tag: Integer, value: Integer): Integer
	events.push(tag)
	return value
end

def probe()
	mut events: Array<Integer> := []
	result := record_value(events, 1, - 5).clamp(record_value(events, 2, - 2), record_value(events, 3, 2))
	puts(result)
	events.each { |item| puts(item) }
	mut maybe: Integer? := nil
	absent := maybe&.clamp(record_value(events, 4, 0), record_value(events, 5, 1))
	puts(absent == nil)
	puts(events.size())
	maybe =- 7
	present := optional_absolute(maybe)
	if present != nil
		puts(present)
	end
	callback := fn(value: Integer): Integer
		return value.abs().clamp(2, 5)
	end
	mapped := [- 7, 1, 3].map { |value| callback(value) }
	mapped.each { |value| puts(value) }
	text := "held" + result.to_s()
	puts(text)
end

callback: Callback
end

absent: Holder? := nil
mut calls := 0
argument := fn(): Integer
calls += 1

end

end

end

def power(exponent: Integer): Float
	mut value := 1.0
	mut index := 0

cases.title: Array keyed ordering: managed narrowed
cases.declarations:
record Entry
	key: String
	value: String
end

def sorted(values: Array<Entry>): Array<Entry>
	return values.sort_by { |entry| entry.key + "!" }
end

def exercise()
	part := "ab"
	entries := [Entry.new(key: part + "c", value: "first"), Entry.new(key: "a", value: "second"), Entry.new(key: part + "c", value: "third")]
	mut result := sorted(entries)
	result.each { |entry| puts(entry.value) }
	result[0] = Entry.new(key: "z", value: "changed")
	puts(entries[1].value)
	read := fn(): String
		return entries.sort_by_descending { |entry| entry.key }[0].value
	end
	puts(read())
	optional: Array<Entry>? := entries
	if optional != nil
		ordered := optional.sort_by { |entry| entry.key }
		puts(ordered[0].value)
	end
	absent: Array<Entry>? := nil
	mut calls := 0
	if absent != nil
		missing := absent.sort_by do |entry|
			calls += 1
			entry.key
		end
		puts(missing.size())
	end
	puts(absent == nil)
	puts(calls)
end

def visit(values: Array<Integer>?): Integer
	mut total := 0
	values&.each.with_index do |value, index|
		if value == 2
			next
		end
		if value == 4
			break
		end
		total += value * 10 + index
	end
	return total
end

def early(values: Range<Integer>?): Integer
	values&.each do |value|
		if value == 2
			return value
		end
	end
	return - 1
end

def entries(values: Hash<String, Integer>?): Integer
	mut total := 0
	values&.each { |key, value| total += key.size() + value }
	return total
end

def source(mut calls: Array<Integer>): Array<Integer>?
	calls.push(1)
	return [4, 5]
end

cases.title: Safe collection transforms
cases.declarations:
def integer_or(value: Integer?, fallback: Integer): Integer
	if value == nil
		return fallback
	end
	return value
end

def truth(value: Boolean?): Boolean
	if value == nil
		return false
	end
	return value
end

def initial(mut calls: Array<Integer>): Integer
	calls.push(10)
	return 10
end

def summarize(values: Array<Integer>?, mut calls: Array<Integer>)
	puts(values&.map { |value| calls.push(value); value + 1 } == nil)
	puts(integer_or(values&.select { |value| value > 1 }&.size(), - 1))
	puts(integer_or(values&.reduce(initial(calls)) { |sum, value| sum + value }, - 1))
	puts(truth(values&.any? { |value| value == 2 }))
	puts(truth(values&.all? { |value| value > 0 }))
	puts(truth(values&.none? { |value| value < 0 }))
	puts(integer_or(values&.find { |value| value == 2 }, - 1))
	puts(integer_or(values&.find_index { |value| value == 2 }, - 1))
	puts(integer_or(values&.sort_by { |value| value % 2 }&.size(), - 1))
	puts(integer_or(values&.sort_by_descending { |value| value }&.size(), - 1))
end

def range_sum(values: Range<Integer>?): Integer?
	return values&.map.with_index { |value, index| value + index }&.reduce(0) { |sum, value| sum + value }
end

cases.title: Maximum JSON nesting and deterministic excess-depth rejection
cases.declarations:
import trb/std/json
import trb/std/result
def inspect(depth: Integer)
mut opening := ""
mut closing := ""
mut index := 0
while index < depth
opening += "["
closing += "]"
index += 1
end
case JSON.parse(opening + "0" + closing)
when Result::Ok(value)
puts("accepted")
case JSON.stringify(value)
when Result::Ok(text)
puts(text.size())
when Result::Err(error)
puts(error.message)
end
when Result::Err(error)
puts(error.message)
puts(error.line)
puts(error.column)
end
end

cases.title: Unicode syntax and escape diagnostics
cases.declarations:
import trb/std/json
import trb/std/jsonc
import trb/std/result
def show_error(error: JSON::Error)
case error.kind
when JSON::ErrorKind::Syntax
puts("Syntax")
when JSON::ErrorKind::Decode
puts("Decode")
when JSON::ErrorKind::Encode
puts("Encode")
end
puts(error.message)
puts(error.path)
if error.line != nil
puts(error.line)
else
puts(-1)
end
if error.column != nil
puts(error.column)
else
puts(-1)
end
end
def show(value: JSON::Value)
case JSON.stringify(value)
when Result::Ok(text)
puts(text)
when Result::Err(error)
show_error(error)
end
end
def probe(source: String)
case JSON.parse(source)
when Result::Ok(value)
show(value)
when Result::Err(error)
show_error(error)
end
end
def comments(source: String)
case JSONC.parse(source)
when Result::Ok(value)
show(value)
when Result::Err(error)
show_error(error)
end
end

import { Body, Headers, HttpMethod } from trb/http
import trb/std/result
def source_name(source: ParameterSource): String
case source
when ParameterSource::Path
return "path"
when ParameterSource::Query
return "query"
end
end
def render_error(error: ParameterError): String
case error
when ParameterError::MalformedQuery(error)
return "malformed:" + error.input
when ParameterError::Missing(source: source, name: name)
return "missing:" + source_name(source) + ":" + name
when ParameterError::Duplicate(source: source, name: name)
return "duplicate:" + source_name(source) + ":" + name
when ParameterError::Invalid(source: source, name: name, value: value, expected: expected)
return "invalid:" + source_name(source) + ":" + name + ":" + value + ":" + expected
end
end

import { Request, RequestError } from trb/web
import { Body, Headers, HttpMethod } from trb/http
record Input
name: String
end
def request_error(error: RequestError): String
case error
when RequestError::MissingContentType
return "missing"
when RequestError::DuplicateContentType
return "duplicate"
when RequestError::UnsupportedContentType(value)
return "unsupported:" + value
when RequestError::InvalidUtf8
return "utf8"
when RequestError::InvalidJson(error)
return error_label(error)
end
end

when Result::Ok(value)
puts(value.name)
when Result::Err(error)
puts(request_error(error))
end

import { Request, RequestError } from trb/web
import { Body, Headers, HttpMethod } from trb/http

end

when RequestError::MissingContentType
return "missing"
when RequestError::DuplicateContentType
return "duplicate"
when RequestError::UnsupportedContentType(value)

when RequestError::InvalidJson(error)

when Result::Err(error)

import { Context, Request, EndpointInputError, ParameterError, ParameterSource, RequestError } from trb/web
import { Body, Header, Headers, HttpMethod } from trb/http
import trb/std/result
def location(source: ParameterSource): String
case source
when ParameterSource::Path
return "path"
when ParameterSource::Query
return "query"
end
end
def parameter(error: ParameterError): String
case error
when ParameterError::MalformedQuery(error)
return "malformed:" + error.input
when ParameterError::Missing(source: source, name: name)
return "missing:" + location(source) + ":" + name
when ParameterError::Duplicate(source: source, name: name)
return "duplicate:" + location(source) + ":" + name
when ParameterError::Invalid(source: source, name: name, value: value, expected: expected)
return "invalid:" + location(source) + ":" + name + ":" + value + ":" + expected
end
end
def request_error(error: RequestError): String
case error
when RequestError::MissingContentType
return "missing-content-type"
when RequestError::DuplicateContentType
return "duplicate-content-type"
when RequestError::UnsupportedContentType(value)
return "unsupported-content-type:" + value
when RequestError::InvalidUtf8
return "invalid-utf8"
when RequestError::InvalidJson(error)
return "json:" + error.path
end
end
def render(error: EndpointInputError): String
case error
when EndpointInputError::Params(error)
return "params:" + parameter(error)
when EndpointInputError::Query(error)
return "query:" + parameter(error)
when EndpointInputError::Body(error)
return "body:" + request_error(error)
end
end
def context(id: String = "7", query: String = "name=kept", body: String = "{\"title\":\"new\"}", content_type: String = "application/json"): Context
return Context.new(request: Request.new(method: HttpMethod.get(), path: "/items/7", query_string: query, headers: Headers.new([Header.new(name: "content-type", value: content_type)]), body: Body.new(body.to_bytes())), path_parameters: {"id": id})
end

id: Integer
end
record QueryInput
name: String
end
record Payload
title: String
end
record Input
params: PathInput
end

puts(value.params.id)

import { Context, ContextKey, Next, Request, Response } from trb/web
import { Body, Header, Headers, HttpMethod } from trb/http
import { RequestID } from trb/web/middleware/request_id
import trb/std/encoding/hex
import trb/std/result
KEY := ContextKey<Integer>.new("counter")
def context_for(headers: Headers): Context
request := Request.new(method: HttpMethod.get(), path: "/example", query_string: "", headers: headers, body: Body.empty())
return Context.new(request: request, path_parameters: {"id" => "7"}).with(KEY, 42)
end
def header_text(context: Context, header: String): String
case context.request.header_value(header)
when Result::Ok(value)
return value
when Result::Err(_error)
return "missing"
end
end
class Terminal implements Next
@header: String
def initialize(header: String)
@header = header
end
def call(context: Context): Response
case context.fetch(KEY)
when Result::Ok(value)
puts(value)
when Result::Err(_error)
puts("missing state")
end
puts(context.path_value("id"))
return Response.text(header_text(context, @header))
end
end
def response_header(response: Response, name: String): String
case response.header_value(name)
when Result::Ok(value)
return value
when Result::Err(_error)
return "missing"
end
end
def generated_response(response: Response, name: String)
text := response.body.to_s()
puts(text.size() == 32)
puts(response_header(response, name) == text)
case Hex.decode(text)
when Result::Ok(value)
puts(value.size() == 16)
when Result::Err(_error)
puts(false)
end
end

def probe()
context := context_for(Headers.new([Header.new(name: "X-Request-ID", value: "abc_123-XYZ=")]))
response := RequestID.call(context, Terminal.new("x-request-id"))
puts(response.body.to_s())
puts(response_header(response, "x-request-id"))
puts(header_text(context, "x-request-id"))
end

import trb/std/encoding/hex
import trb/std/result
KEY := ContextKey<Integer>.new("counter")
def context_for(headers: Headers): Context
request := Request.new(method: HttpMethod.get(), path: "/example", query_string: "", headers: headers, body: Body.empty())
return Context.new(request: request, path_parameters: {"id" => "7"}).with(KEY, 42)
end
def header_text(context: Context, header: String): String
case context.request.header_value(header)
when Result::Ok(value)
return value
when Result::Err(_error)
return "missing"
end
end
class Terminal implements Next
@header: String
def initialize(header: String)
@header = header
end
def call(context: Context): Response
case context.fetch(KEY)
when Result::Ok(value)
puts(value)
when Result::Err(_error)
puts("missing state")
end
puts(context.path_value("id"))
return Response.text(header_text(context, @header))
end
end
def response_header(response: Response, name: String): String
case response.header_value(name)
when Result::Ok(value)
return value
when Result::Err(_error)
return "missing"
end
end
def generated_response(response: Response, name: String)
text := response.body.to_s()
puts(text.size() == 32)
puts(response_header(response, name) == text)
case Hex.decode(text)
when Result::Ok(value)
puts(value.size() == 16)
when Result::Err(_error)
puts(false)
end
end

def probe()
["too-long", "é", "", "a b"].each do |candidate|
context := context_for(Headers.new([Header.new(name: "x-request-id", value: candidate)]))
options := RequestIDOptions.new(header_name: "x-request-id", limit_length: 3)
generated_response(RequestID.call(context, Terminal.new("x-request-id"), options), "x-request-id")
end
end

cases.title: Encodings and request ID: request id limit zero
cases.declarations:
import { Context, ContextKey, Next, Request, Response } from trb/web
import { Body, Header, Headers, HttpMethod } from trb/http
import { RequestID, RequestIDOptions } from trb/web/middleware/request_id
import trb/std/encoding/hex
import trb/std/result
KEY := ContextKey<Integer>.new("counter")
def context_for(headers: Headers): Context
request := Request.new(method: HttpMethod.get(), path: "/example", query_string: "", headers: headers, body: Body.empty())
return Context.new(request: request, path_parameters: {"id" => "7"}).with(KEY, 42)
end
def header_text(context: Context, header: String): String
case context.request.header_value(header)
when Result::Ok(value)
return value
when Result::Err(_error)
return "missing"
end
end
class Terminal implements Next
@header: String
def initialize(header: String)
@header = header
end
def call(context: Context): Response
case context.fetch(KEY)
when Result::Ok(value)
puts(value)
when Result::Err(_error)
puts("missing state")
end
puts(context.path_value("id"))
return Response.text(header_text(context, @header))
end
end
def response_header(response: Response, name: String): String
case response.header_value(name)
when Result::Ok(value)
return value
when Result::Err(_error)
return "missing"
end
end
def generated_response(response: Response, name: String)
text := response.body.to_s()
puts(text.size() == 32)
puts(response_header(response, name) == text)
case Hex.decode(text)
when Result::Ok(value)
puts(value.size() == 16)
when Result::Err(_error)
puts(false)
end
end

def probe()
context := context_for(Headers.new([Header.new(name: "x-request-id", value: "a")]))
options := RequestIDOptions.new(header_name: "x-request-id", limit_length: 0)
response := RequestID.call(context, Terminal.new("x-request-id"), options)
generated_response(response, "x-request-id")
end

cases.title: Path values: record and collection retention across allocations
cases.declarations:
import { Path, RelativePath } from trb/std/path
import trb/std/result
record Box
path: RelativePath
end
cases.body:
case RelativePath.parse("first")
when Result::Ok(path)
mut paths: Array<RelativePath> := [path]
mut index := 0
while index < 500
case path.child(index.to_s())
when Result::Ok(child)
paths.push(child)
when Result::Err(error)
puts(error.to_s())
end
index += 1
end
puts(paths[0].to_s())
puts(paths[500].to_s())
box := Box.new(path: paths[500])
puts(Path.new("root").join(box.path).to_s())
when Result::Err(error)
puts("error:" + error.to_s())
end

cases.title: StringBuilder boundaries
cases.declarations:
import trb/std/string_builder

def extend(mut writer: StringBuilder)
	writer.append("!")
end

def probe()
	mut writer := StringBuilder.from_string("A")
	mut shared := writer
	writer.append("\xf0\x9f")
	puts(writer.size())
	early := writer.to_s()
	shared.append("\x98\x80")
	extend(shared)
	snapshot := writer.to_s()
	puts(snapshot)
	puts(writer.size())
	puts(early.to_bytes().size())
	writer.clear()
	puts(writer.empty?())
	writer.append_codepoint(12354)
	writer.append_codepoint(0)
	writer.append("Z")
	puts(writer.size())
	puts(writer.to_s().to_bytes().size())
	puts(snapshot)
	puts(shared.to_s() == writer.to_s())
	mut separate := StringBuilder.new()
	separate.append("x")
	puts(writer.size())
end

cases.title: StringBuilder growth
cases.declarations:
import trb/std/string_builder

record Held
	writer: StringBuilder
	text: String
end

def update(mut writer: StringBuilder, count: Integer)
	mut i := 0
	while i < count
		writer.append("a😀")
		i += 1
	end
end

def probe()
	mut writer := StringBuilder.new()
	update(writer, 1024)
	snapshot := writer.to_s()
	held := Held.new(writer: writer, text: snapshot)
	mut writers := [writer]
	mut shared := writers[0]
	update(shared, 1024)
	puts(held.text.size())
	puts(writer.size())
	puts(held.writer.to_s().to_bytes().size())
	writer.clear()
	writer.append("after")
	puts(held.text.size())
	puts(held.writer.to_s())
	mut retained: Array<String> := []
	mut i := 0
	while i < 512
		mut item := StringBuilder.from_string("saved-")
		item.append(i.to_s())
		retained.push(item.to_s())
		item.clear()
		item.append("changed")
		i += 1
	end
	puts(retained[0])
	puts(retained[511])
end

end
